evidence.curator_note: First half of Equation 8.81 (arrow labelled 'rH'). The drawn substrate is a fatty-acid methyl ester carrying a phenyl group at C-6 (the running text: 'very useful for identifying substitution at C-6 in fatty-acid methyl esters'); as drawn the phenyl-bearing carbon also carries an explicit H and no further chain, i.e. methyl 6-phenylhexanoate, and that concrete instantiation is what is encoded here. The molecular ion is drawn n-ionized on the ESTER ALKOXY oxygen ('+.' printed on the O of OCH3), not on the carbonyl oxygen, and the benzylic epsilon-H is transferred to it through the large (7-membered) ring transition state that the page draws; the text calls this 'an epsilon-H rearrangement'. Book draws 2 arcs; moves <1,2> are drawn (a fishhook from the O+. odd electron pointing at the migrating H, and a fishhook from the benzylic C-H bond pointing at the O), move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page) - the second C-H electron stays on C-6, which is why the next structure is drawn with a '.' on the benzylic carbon. Product is the distonic ion: benzylic radical plus a closed-shell trialkyl/protonated oxonium O+(H)(CH3)C(=O).

Second half of Equation 8.81 (arrow labelled 'rd', McLafferty's radical-site displacement). Net change read off the two drawn structures: the benzylic radical closes to the C5=C6 double bond, the H on C-5 migrates to the ester carbon C-1 through a six-membered arrangement, and the O-protonated methoxy group leaves as neutral CH3OH, so the charge and the odd electron end up on the (former) carbonyl oxygen of the drawn (M - CH3OH)+. enal ion. Book draws 5 arcs; moves <1,2,3,4,5> are ALL drawn - no implicit hook is needed. Arc-by-arc: <1> fishhook from the '.' on C-6 to the C5-C6 bond; <2> fishhook from the C5-H bond to the same forming pi bond; <3> long fishhook from the C5-H bond sweeping across the ring toward C-1 (the migrating H with one electron); <4> long arc drawn with its tail on/under the C1=O carbonyl bond and its head pointing at the migrating H - encoded as a nonbonding electron of the carbonyl oxygen entering the new C1-H bond, because the drawn product retains a full C=O double bond and puts '+.' on that oxygen; taking arc <4>'s tail literally as the C=O pi pair would reduce the C=O bond order, which the drawn product does not show; <5> arrow with a solid (two-barbed) head from the C1-O(methyl) bond to that oxygen - encoded as the full 2-electron heterolysis that the drawn CLOSED-SHELL neutral HOCH3 requires (a homolytic split would give CH3OH+.). Chemical caveat: this is a heavily concerted depiction (pi-bond formation, H migration and C-O cleavage in one step); the book gives no intermediate for it, so no intermediate state is invented here.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.81 (its chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14, the German-edition numbering), so no MØD rule variable is cross-linked to this scheme. Verified rather than assumed: the only chapter-8 ester rules in the index, IMS_8_9_1_OCH3 and IMS_8_9_2_OCH3, encode an H rearrangement onto the CARBONYL O+. of an alpha,beta-unsaturated methyl ester followed by alpha cleavage to the dienol ion ([_A]1[C]2[C]3([H]4)[C]5{=}[C]6[C]7([O]8[C]9...){=}[O+.]13 >> ... [O+.]13([H]4)); they neither ionize the alkoxy oxygen nor break the C(acyl)-OCH3 bond, so they do NOT describe Equation 8.81 and are not cross-linked. Loss of CH3OH from an ester is not represented by any indexed rule.

The page prints NO numeric m/z and NO intensity anywhere in Equation 8.81. The prose states that the epsilon-H rearrangement yields '(M - CH3OH)+. and (M - 76)+. peaks (Meyerson and Leitch 1966) that are very useful for identifying substitution at C-6 in fatty-acid methyl esters', which is the book's assertion that the ion is observed; detected=true rests on that sentence only. observed_mz 174.1039 is curator-computed (C12H14O+., monoisotopic mass of the cation with the electron mass subtracted) for the drawn methyl 6-phenylhexanoate instantiation (M+. = 206.1301), NOT a measured value from the book, and relative_intensity is therefore omitted. For a longer 6-phenyl fatty-acid ester the loss is still CH3OH (32) but the absolute m/z shifts. The page itself names no ionization or activation experiment and prints no electron energy; ms_context follows the book's standard 70 eV EI convention for an intact molecular ion.
